Hi Olivia / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the sync today. Good to align on ACME's primary use cases (customer support triage + internal knowledge base search) and the expected 50k monthly active queries distribution across US and EU. Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

Summary of decisions from the call:
- Primary runtime: Redwood hosted API for POC, with Dedicated reserved capacity for high-throughput routes if we hit SLA requirements.
- Integration priorities: SDK setup & auth, structured outputs for tool-calling, embeddings + reranker for KB retrieval, and model routing policies to balance latency/cost.

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
1) Redwood to share SDK quickstart and integration diagram (Dev) — target: 7/20 (attached).
2) ACME to share a sample KB dataset + privacy checklist for embeddings tests (ACME) — target: 7/24.
3) Tech deep-dive: 45m session to walk SDK auth flow, model routing, and fallback policy — propose Wed 7/22 10:00 ET.
4) Commercial: Marcus to share a ballpark committed pricing for Dedicated capacity and latency-backed SLAs — target: 7/21.

Technical notes we covered that we'll document in the deep-dive:
- SDK & auth: standard API keys for POC; recommend scoped service accounts + KMS-backed keys for Dedicated/Private.
- Routing/policy: ability to route by region, latency SLO, and cost tier. Fallback chains supported (e.g., small model -> mid -> large) with automatic quality check thresholds.
- Structured outputs/tool calling: Redwoods supports function/tool calling and JSON schema enforcement; we can return a structured action (tool name + args) for your orchestration layer.
- Embeddings/rerankers: recommend 2-stage retrieval (dense embeddings for recall + lightweight reranker for precision).

I've attached the SDK quickstart and an integration diagram. Dev, please add any technical clarifications below.

Hi Olivia / Rajiv — jumping in with the technical detail so we can hit the deep-dive with concrete config suggestions. TL;DR: yes to p95-based routing, region-aware fallbacks, and privacy controls for embeddings. Details below and I'll walk through samples in the session.

1) SDK setup & Auth
- Quickstart: see attached redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf. We have JavaScript, Python, and Go clients.
- Auth patterns: 
  - POC: standard API keys scoped to the project.
  - Prod: service accounts + OAuth for short-lived tokens + KMS for key rotation.
  - Private/Dedicated: support for customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations.

2) Model routing recommendations (config snippet we'll demo):
- Primary routing rule: route by region header (us-east / eu-west).
- Latency policy: evaluate p95 latency collected by route; if p95 > 300ms, failover to next model in chain. You mentioned p95 < 250ms target; we can set a conservative threshold at 300ms for POC and tighten under Dedicated.
- Cost policy: attach cost bucket tags to models (low/mid/high). Policies can prefer low-cost models for non-critical paths and only escalate on quality/fallback triggers.
- Fallback chain: small (quantized) -> medium (float16) -> large (standard). You can also create region-specific fallback (e.g., eu-west small -> eu-west medium -> us-east large if eu resources saturated).

3) Structured output & tool calling
- We support function/tool calling with schema enforcement. Example: return JSON {"tool":"kb_fetch","args":{"query":"...","top_k":5}} and Redwood will surface that as a structured action in the SDK response.
- We'll demo how to validate / sanitize tool args before invocation and how to log tool calls for auditing.

4) Embeddings & reranker flow
- Recommended: dense-embedding index for retrieval (e.g., 384-d vector) stored in your vector DB + lightweight reranker model hosted on Redwood for top-10 re-rank.
- Privacy: embeddings are one-way vectors; however we offer a PII detection pre-filter and can opt-out of retention for embeddings created under your account. We support retention windows and deletion APIs.

5) Sample config (pseudo YAML) we'll share in the session and push to your repo after the call. It will include: region routing rules, p95 latency thresholds, cost buckets, fallback chains, and dedup / caching TTLs.

Attachments included in this thread: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (code snippets), acme-integration-diagram.png (network flow). I'll bring the sample YAML to the deep-dive.
